summary:
Leaders: generalist European VCs now lead robotics deals - Creandum (Sereact A, Machenta seed), Headline (Sereact B), HV Capital/Speedinvest (ARX), Elaia (mimic), Lingotto (RobCo, NEURA); the mega-rounds (NEURA $1.4B, Agile Robots $500M, Gravis $200M) are led by non-European money (SoftBank, Tether, Nvidia, Amazon).
Money: 2026 is a record year for European robotics: unicorns Gravis, Humanoid, RobCo; largest Series A (THEKER $85M) and largest UK robotics seed (Machenta $40M).
Demand: investors fund robot brains (Sereact Cortex 2, Machenta one-shot learning, mimic dexterous hands, Flexion) plus logistics (Dexory, Nomagic) and defence (ARX, Quantum Systems).
Public money matters: EIC Fund/Accelerator, EBRD, NATO Innovation Fund and British Business Bank co-invest in robotics but are not realistic partners for a student lab.
Best entry point: Paris-reachable investors whose portfolios match our robot-learning wedge (Elaia, Cathay Innovation, Speedinvest Paris, Creandum) as speakers/demo-day jurors, then intros to their portfolio startups for hardware and mentoring.
